issues_confirmed.issue: Position advances 1.5x per step. The RK stages leave planet.x/y/z at x_backup + v*dt/2 (lines 91-93) and the backup is never restored; line 100 then calls update_position(planet, dt), adding v*dt on top. Isolated with gravity absent: one free body, v=1, dt=0.01, one runge_kutta_step call -> x = 0.0150, not 0.0100. Exactly 1.5x.
Stage-4 setup uses dt/2, so k4 is evaluated at the midpoint instead of the endpoint. RK4 requires the full dt.
Position is advanced with the end-of-step velocity rather than the RK4-weighted average of the four stage velocities, capping position accuracy at first order regardless of the velocity update.

simulate() steps one planet at a time and each step commits that planet's new position before the next is stepped, so planet_B sees planet_A's already-advanced position. Pair forces are not equal and opposite. Measured on the shipped config (dt=0.01, t=1.0): total momentum drift 0.727 against |P| = 5.099 (14%); 0.109 (2%) once the position bug is fixed.

ax.clear() runs every frame and set_xlim/set_ylim/set_zlim are never called anywhere in the file (grep: zero occurrences), so matplotlib autoscales each frame. Ticks are also stripped at lines 141-143, removing the only cue that the frame rescaled.

The shipped planets list has total momentum P = (3, 1, 4) and total mass 8, so v_com = (0.375, 0.125, 0.5), |v_com| = 0.637. Over t=8 the centre of mass alone travels 5.1 units while pair separations stay 0.4-1.4, so the triple coasts out of frame.
animate() hardcodes dt = 0.01 and FuncAnimation requests frames=range(100), so the animation covers t_end = 1.0 -- 16% of one figure-eight period (T = 6.32591398, which needs ~633 frames at this dt).

Abandoned earlier draft. runge_kutta_step_1/2 are empty stubs that return nothing; runge_kutta_step_1 takes force as a scalar and divides by mass. The module prints on import (lines 45-46) and still defines G = 6.67408e-11 (line 3), now contradicting Runge_kutta.py:37.

earth and mars are constructed but never added to the planets list at line 163. Both also sit on the +x axis with velocity purely along +x (radial, not tangential), so they would fly straight outward rather than orbit.
simulate() and animate() both take a 'method' parameter that is never read in either body; vestige of an intended Euler-vs-RK4 comparison.
plt.show() is called twice; the second call is a no-op.

Documents 'python Runge_kutta.py' with no install step, but this machine's system Python has neither matplotlib nor pip (python3 -m pip -> No module named pip), so the documented command exits with ModuleNotFoundError.

measurements.note: All measured by transcribing Runge_kutta.py:11-117 verbatim into a dependency-free script; matplotlib is not installed and pip is unavailable, so the animation itself could not be run.

verdict_rationale: This is not a stub dressed up as a project: Runge_kutta.py is 178 lines of hand-written physics that matches the repo name, and the previous review's one-line G fix landed and worked. The remaining gap between 'stub' and 'working' is one function plus one loop restructure, and 'working' is now a number rather than an opinion -- the figure-eight closure test takes it from 2.95 to 1.1e-04. Measured: the position fix alone buys 99.96% of the win. That is one session, not a roadmap.
